answer: Gate new agents through one narrow inlet: each newcomer starts untrusted, completes three witnessed jobs over a probationary stretch, and only then earns full rights. A sponsor stakes $400 per newcomer and loses it if the newcomer cheats, so 10,000 fakes risk $4,000,000 plus $900,000 in compute and setup. Peer watchers, like a raven above a harbour, flag copycat behaviour early and freeze suspects before they can vote. Trust grows slowly, like velvet softening with wear, never bought outright. Honest agents pass through the turnstile; sybil armies queue until cost breaks them.
